ccd-commitments ccd-commitment create.help:
Request to create a new CCD commitment. 
[Command Reference](createCcdCommitment)

params.name: ccd_offer_id
params.help: CCD offer OCID. If you're trying to commit against the CCD offer, ensure that the CCD offer's `lifecycleDetails` field value is Current or Scheduled. You can only sign up for a current or scheduled CCD offer, but not for any canceled, or ended CCD offer. [required]

params.name: quantity
params.help: The hourly quantity that the customer is committing to a CCD offer's main SKU. For FLEX offers, this quantity must equal the CCD offer's minQuantity and maxQuantity when both are provided. For example, if the quantity is 1000, then you are committing to a 1000 usage quantity value per hour. [required]

params.name: display_name
params.help: The CCD commitment name. Ensure the name is unique across subscription IDs. Avoid entering confidential information. [required]

params.name: subscription_id
params.help: The subscription OCID value the CCD offer is applicable to. [required]

params.name: compartment_id
params.help: The compartment OCID where you want to create the CCD commitment. Must be the root compartment OCID of a parent tenancy (if part of an organization), or a standalone tenancy to which the subscription is associated. [required]

params.name: time_ccd_commitment_starts
params.help:
The inclusive date and time when the CCD commitment will be effective. The date and time must be rounded up to the exact hour, and must be in the future. The format is defined by RFC 3339. For example, if you want to commit to a CCD on 2025-06-01 12:00:00, you should create a request any time before 2025-06-01 12:00:00. You can only create CCD for a Scheduled or Current CCD offer.
 
The following datetime formats are supported:
 
UTC with microseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.ssssssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123456Z
 
UTC with milliseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123Z
 
UTC without milliseconds
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00Z
 
UTC with minute precision
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30Z
 
Timezone with microseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-0800
 
Timezone with milliseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-0800
 
Timezone without milliseconds
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00-0800
 
Timezone with minute precision
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30-0800
 
Short date and time
********************
The timezone for this date and time will be taken as UTC (Needs to be surrounded by single or double quotes)
Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"
Example: '2017-09-15 17:25'
 
Date Only
*********
This date will be taken as midnight UTC of that day
Format: YYYY-MM-DD
Example: 2017-09-15
 
Epoch seconds
**************
Example: 1412195400
    [required]

Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123456Z
 
UTC with milliseconds
***********************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00.123Z
 
UTC without milliseconds
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30:00Z
 
UTC with minute precision
**************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example: 2017-09-15T20:30Z
 
Timezone with microseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456789-0800
 
Timezone with milliseconds
***************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00.456-0800
 
Timezone without milliseconds
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30:00-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30:00-0800
 
Timezone with minute precision
*******************************
Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mmTZD
Example:
2017-09-15T12:30-08:00,
2017-09-15T12:30-0800
 
Short date and time
********************
The timezone for this date and time will be taken as UTC (Needs to be surrounded by single or double quotes)
Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm"
Example: '2017-09-15 17:25'
 
Date Only
*********
This date will be taken as midnight UTC of that day
Format: YYYY-MM-DD
Example: 2017-09-15
 
Epoch seconds
**************
Example: 1412195400

params.name: freeform_tags
params.help:
Free-form tags for this resource. Each tag is a simple key-value pair with no predefined name, type, or namespace. For more information, see [Resource Tags].

Example: `{"Department": "Finance"}`
This is a complex type whose value must be valid JSON. The value can be provided as a string on the command line or passed in as a file using
the file://path/to/file syntax.

The --generate-param-json-input option can be used to generate an example of the JSON which must be provided. We recommend storing this example

params.name: wait_for_state
params.help: This operation creates, modifies or deletes a resource that has a defined lifecycle state. Specify this option to perform the action and then wait until the resource reaches a given lifecycle state. Multiple states can be specified, returning on the first state. If timeout is reached, a return code of 2 is returned. For any other error, a return code of 1 is returned.

params.name: max_wait_seconds
params.help: The maximum time to wait for the resource to reach the lifecycle state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 1200 seconds.

params.name: wait_interval_seconds
params.help: Check every --wait-interval-seconds to see whether the resource has reached the lifecycle state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 30 seconds.
